What does a Fractional AI Lead cost and who is the role for?

Fractional AI Lead from Dave Willemstein gives organizations with running AI initiatives but no clear owner senior AI leadership on a part-time basis. The role is priced as a fixed monthly fee, depending on the level: Advice, Lead or Lead+. The minimum term is 3 months and the role is cancellable monthly after that; all proposals are excluding VAT and travel expenses.
When can a Fractional AI Lead be cancelled?
Fractional AI Lead runs for a minimum of 3 months and is cancellable monthly after that.
Is the Fractional AI Lead a full-time role?
Fractional AI Lead is senior leadership on a part-time basis, for 2, 4 or 8 days per month, not a full-time role. It fits teams that need direction and capacity but cannot yet carry a full-time role.
Source: Dave Willemstein's rates and typical timelines. Updated: October 2026.

Manufacturer brought scattered pilots under one roadmap.

At an international manufacturing organization, seven pilots were running across four countries with no connection between them. In nine months that became one approved roadmap, three applications scaled, and an internal lead who took it over.
7separate pilots at the start3applications scaled25%productivity target set9months to handover
Answers to what you are thinking now.
How many days do I need?+

Two days a month works if a strategy is in place and execution mainly needs safeguarding. Four days is more realistic if governance still needs to be built, or if multiple business units are involved.
Are you available between the fixed days?+
Yes, for escalations and short questions. That is included in the rate. What is not included is unlimited attendance at meetings: nobody benefits from that.
What happens if we hire someone internally?+
Then my work has succeeded. I help with the job profile and selection, and scale down to a sparring role. We build the handover plan in month one, not month six.
Do you work with multiple clients at once?+
Yes, a maximum of three fractional roles in parallel. Never two direct competitors, and I check that before accepting an assignment.
